citations.short: Buildings not maintained in good state of repair
citations.long: Buildings used in the manufacturing, processing, packing, and holding of a drug product are not maintained in a good state of repair.
Equipment and utensils are not cleaned at appropriate intervals to prevent contamination that would alter the safety, identity, strength, quality or purity of the drug product.
Written procedures are not established and followed for the cleaning and maintenance of equipment, including utensils, used in the manufacture, processing, packing or holding of a drug product.
Written production and process control procedures are not followed in the execution of production and process control functions.

citations.short: Procedures not  in writing, fully followed
citations.long: The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing.
Aseptic processing areas are deficient regarding the system for cleaning and disinfecting the room to produce aseptic conditions.

citations.short: Written records kept in individual logs
citations.long: Written records of major equipment cleaning, maintenance, and use are not included in individual equipment logs.

The master production and control records are deficient in that they do not include complete manufacturing, control, instructions, sampling, testing, procedures, specifications, special notations, and precautions.

citations.short: Buildings of Suitable Size, Construction, Location
citations.long: Buildings used in the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of a drug product do not have the suitable construction to facilitate cleaning, maintenance, and proper operations.

citations.short: Components withheld from use pending release
citations.long: Each lot of components, drug product containers, and closures is not withheld from use until the lot has been sampled, tested, examined, and released by the quality control unit.

Laboratory controls do not include the establishment of scientifically sound and appropriate test procedures designed to assure that in-process materials conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality and purity.
There is a failure to thoroughly review any unexplained discrepancy whether or not the batch has been already distributed.
Employees engaged in the manufacture of a drug product lack the training required to perform their assigned functions.

citations.short: Product flow through building is inadequate
citations.long: The flow of components, drug product containers, closures, labeling, in-process materials, and drug products though the building is not designed to prevent contamination.
Equipment for adequate control over temperature is not provided when appropriate for the manufacture, processing, packing or holding of a drug product.

citations.short: Buildings not maintained in good state of repair
citations.long: Buildings used in the manufacturing, processing, packing, and holding of a drug product are not maintained in a good state of repair.
Equipment used in the manufacture, processing, packing or holding of drug products is not of appropriate design, of adequate size, and suitably located to facilitate operations for its intended use.
Equipment and utensils are not cleaned at appropriate intervals to prevent contamination that would alter the safety, identity, strength, quality or purity of the drug product.
Routine calibration of mechanical equipment is not performed according to a written program designed to assure proper performance.

citations.short: Written calibration / inspection records not  kept
citations.long: Records of the calibration checks and inspections of automatic, mechanical or electronic equipment, including computers or related systems are not maintained.

Written procedures are lacking which describe in sufficient detail the receipt, identification, storage, handling, sampling, testing, approval, and rejection of components, drug product containers, and closures.

citations.short: Handling and Storage to Prevent Contamination
citations.long: There was a failure to handle and store components at all times in a manner to prevent contamination.
Representative samples are not taken of each shipment of each lot of components, drug product containers, and closures for testing or examination.
Drug product closures were not sterilized and processed to remove pyrogenic properties to assure that they are suitable for their intended use.

There are no written procedures for production and process controls designed to assure that the drug products have the identity, strength, quality, and purity they purport or are represented to possess.

citations.short: Control procedures to monitor and validate performance
citations.long: Control procedures are not established which monitor the output and validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product.

Laboratory controls do not include the establishment of scientifically sound and appropriate test procedures designed to assure that in-process materials conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality and purity.

Testing and release of drug product for distribution do not include appropriate laboratory determination of satisfactory conformance to the final specifications and identity and strength of each active ingredient prior to release.
The accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and reproducibility of test methods have not been established.
The batch production and control records are deficient in that they do not include in-process and laboratory control results.
There is a failure to thoroughly review any unexplained discrepancy whether or not the batch has been already distributed.
